steps.title: Key Context
steps.body: The Spanish Armada of 1588 was the culmination of decades of growing tension between England and Spain. Philip II of Spain, the most powerful monarch in Europe, was motivated by a combination of religious, political, and economic grievances against Elizabeth I. The execution of Mary Queen of Scots in February 1587 gave Philip the final justification he needed.

steps.title: Weaknesses of the Armada
steps.body: Despite its size, the Armada had significant weaknesses: (1) the original commander, the Marquis of Santa Cruz, died in February 1588 and was replaced by Medina Sidonia, who had no naval experience; (2) Drake's raid on Cadiz (1587) had destroyed supplies and delayed the fleet; (3) many of the ships were armed merchant vessels, not purpose-built warships; (4) the Spanish ships were designed for boarding and close combat, not long-range gunnery; (5) the plan required perfect coordination between the Armada and Parma's army, which was extremely difficult in an era before radio communication.

steps.title: 1. Better Tactics and Ships
steps.body: The English ships were smaller, faster, and more manoeuvrable than the Spanish galleons. They could sail closer to the wind and choose their position in battle. English guns had longer range and could fire faster - the English used a "stand-off" tactic, pounding the Spanish from a distance, while the Spanish were designed for close boarding actions. The English fired approximately 2,000 rounds at Gravelines, compared to approximately 750 from the Spanish.

steps.title: 2. Better Commanders
steps.body: The English were led by Lord Howard of Effingham (Lord High Admiral), with experienced seamen like Sir Francis Drake, Sir John Hawkins, and Martin Frobisher under his command. They understood naval warfare and adapted their tactics to the situation. The Spanish commander, the Duke of Medina Sidonia, had no naval experience and had begged Philip not to appoint him.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always use specific dates: Armada spotted 19 July 1588 , fire ships 28 July , Gravelines 29 July Know the numbers: 130 ships, 30,000 men in the Armada; 67 ships, 15,000 men lost Explain the causes in categories: religious, political, economic For "reasons for victory" questions, discuss multiple factors (tactics, ships, commanders, weather, Spanish errors) Remember Elizabeth's Tilbury speech - it's useful for questions about her image and leadership The phrase "God breathed and they were scattered" shows how the victory was interpreted as divine favour Link the Armada to earlier events: the Dutch revolt, Drake's raids, Mary's execution
